subject: RFP: stability gates and traffic-shift procedures for LuminaBank integration
messages:

Hi Logan,

Thanks for pinging us last week at the vendor fair. The procurement and platform teams here at Lumina have been reviewing Redwood's RFP response and we'd like a focused writeup on your recommended production cutover and rollback controls for our payments fraud model integration. In particular, the security and platform owners asked for a section that details:

- stability gates (metrics and pass/fail thresholds) we should verify before 100% traffic shift
- canary ramp steps and durations for low-latency SLA targets
- integration steps for tokenization and audit logging so we can meet our compliance windows
- runbooks for automated circuit-breaker / graceful degradation (how do you fallback to cheaper variants?)

Can you share a short implementation/migration timeline and the operational checks your team recommends? We need this for the next procurement review on May 3.

Best,
Sam
Sam Roberts
Senior Procurement Manager
Lumina Bank

Attachments: redwood-rollout-gates-v1.pdf (application/pdf)

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear ask and the RFP doc. Attached is a concise implementation and cutover proposal tailored to the fraud model use case. Highlights up front:

- Canary plan: 0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%, with automated health checks after each step (5-minute steady-state for <50ms p50 latency; error-rate <0.2%). Each ramp step is nominally 30 minutes but can be extended by the on-call engineer.
- Stability gates: p50/p95 latency, error-rate, model-score drift (KL divergence on core scoring features), end-to-end transaction latency, and audit log completeness. Pass/fail thresholds are listed in the attached PDF.
- Traffic-shift controls: header-based routing (X-RW-Canary), progressive traffic split managed by Redwood's routing policy engine, and a manual abort + automatic fallback to a compatible quantized variant if latency or error thresholds breach.
- Rollback & graceful degradation: automatic fallback tiers (full model -> quantized model -> small embedding-only rerank) with soft-degradation messages returned to the caller and automatic alerting to your SREs.
- Audit & compliance: all inference requests are logged (request id, model id, input hash, output signature), stored in your VPC audit bucket with retention controls. We propose 90-day hot retention + 365-day cold archive; we can extend to match Lumina's retention policy.

We included a short timeline and a set of runbook steps in the PDF. Two asks for your team to close the procurement review:
1) Confirm whether your SREs want us to run a staged test on a copy of production traffic or on synthetic replay.
2) Confirm desired commit windows (we typically expect a 4-hour maintenance window for the 25%->100% jump on first rollout).

If helpful, Marissa can walk through the runbook in a 30-minute session next week.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: Lumina cutover checklist & owner map

Team — following up on Sam's ask and Logan's draft: I mapped owners and modified a few of the gates to be more conservative given it's a payments workload. Key notes:

- Owner map:
  - Pre-cutover verification: Aditya (integration & auth), Priyom (canary automation), Logan (on-call for first two ramps)
  - Monitoring & alerts: Marissa (console dashboards) + Lumina SRE contact (Erika)
- Additional stability gates we added:
  - Audit log ingestion lag < 2 minutes for first 24 hours post-rollout
  - Model-score drift alarm if KL divergence > 0.08 over a 1-hour window
  - Transaction-level reconciliation mismatch rate < 0.01%
- Canary timing: change to 45-minute verification at 25% on first rollout; subsequent rollouts can use the default 30-minute windows.
- Circuit-breaker thresholds: error-rate 0.15% (hard abort), latency p95 300ms (soft throttle + alert). If a hard abort occurs we immediately shift to the quantized variant and open a P0 with Lumina SREs.

Action items:
- Aditya: produce an auth/tokenization sequence diagram and confirm whether Lumina will require request-level token binding (deadline: 2027-05-10).
- Priyom: add automated canary rollback steps to the runbook and include the exact CLI commands for opsim. (deadline: 2027-05-12)
- Logan: Schedule the 30-minute review with Lumina for May 18 or 19.

I'll assemble the updated runbook and push a PDF to the shared Drive once the owner items are in.

Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Hi Sam / Erika — thanks for the time on the call yesterday. Per our discussion, attached is the runbook (MD) and the updated rollout gates PDF has been uploaded to the Drive link below. TL;DR proposed schedule below:

- Week 0 (prep): entitlement & KMS setup; token binding test; test account shadowing (2 business days)
- Week 1 (integration tests): end-to-end with synthetic traffic; audit ingestion validation (3 business days)
- Week 2 (staged cutover):
  - Day 1: Canary 1% (30m, automated checks)
  - Day 2: Canary 5% (30m)
  - Day 3: Canary 25% (45m verification)
  - Day 4: 100% (maintenance window; final verification)
- Post-cutover (2 weeks): intensified monitoring, daily reconciliation, lowered thresholds for alerts, and SLA review meeting.

Operational controls we covered:
- Header-based routing + routing policy priority for region and tier, with built-in fallback to the lowest-cost compatible model if any gate fails.
- Automated rollback that triggers a gradual traffic shift back to the previous stable variant over 10 minutes, with a one-click abort in the Redwood Console.
- Audit log delivery guarantees to your VPC bucket with checksum validation and delivery receipts.
- Canary telemetry: p50/p95 latency, error-rate, model-score drift, request-to-response time, and a synthetic probe that validates transaction-level correctness.

Next steps for Lumina: please confirm whether you prefer synthetic replay or live shadowing for Week 1 by EOD May 30. Once confirmed we will book the maintenance window and share final runbook commands.
